content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Choose how much for uncountable nouns and how many for countable nouns. Model: “How many bananas do you need, and how much rice do you want?” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use how much and how many clearly and politely. One useful response is: “How many bananas do you need, and how much rice do you want?” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where how much and how many is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about how much and how many.

language_focus: Choose how much for uncountable nouns and how many for countable nouns.
objectives: Choose how much for uncountable nouns and how many for countable nouns.
Use asking about quantity in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about how much and how many.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about how much and how many. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: How many bottles do they need?
listening.transcript: How much water do we need? We need two bottles.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Say how MUCH and how MAN-y with stress on the last word. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Say how MUCH and how MAN-y with stress on the last word.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about how much and how many.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using how much and how many; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise how much and how many?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: How many bananas do you need, and how much rice do you want?

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about how much and how many with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about how much and how many. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: How many bananas do you need, and how much rice do you want? Submit your draft first.
